title: Tech Startup Builder: Design Your App
description: Build a complete tech startup by dragging the right components into the correct architecture slots. Design a mobile app from frontend to backend, database to deployment. Learn how real-world tech stacks are assembled and understand the role each layer plays in powering the apps you use every day -- from Zomato to Paytm.
learning_objectives: Understand the layered architecture of a modern tech startup's application stack, from user interface to deployment
Learn the role of frontend frameworks like React and Flutter in creating interactive user experiences on web and mobile
Recognise why backend APIs built with Node.js or Python are essential for processing business logic and serving data
Understand how databases like PostgreSQL and MongoDB store, organise, and retrieve application data reliably
Learn the importance of authentication and security layers (OAuth, JWT) in protecting user data and preventing unauthorised access
Explore how cloud infrastructure providers like AWS and GCP enable startups to scale globally without managing physical servers
Understand the role of payment gateways like Razorpay and Stripe in enabling secure online transactions and monetisation
Discover how analytics dashboards provide actionable business insights by tracking user behaviour, engagement, and revenue metrics
Learn how CI/CD pipelines automate the software development lifecycle from code commit to production deployment

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read the description of each empty architecture slot carefully -- it describes the function that layer performs in the tech stack
Examine the 8 draggable technology components in the parts tray and understand what each one does by reading its description
Drag a component from the parts tray and drop it into the architecture slot where you think it belongs
If you place the correct component, the slot activates with a green glow and you earn 15 points
If the component is wrong, you lose 5 points and receive a hint -- read it carefully and try a different component
Place all 8 components correctly within the 3-minute time limit to fully assemble your tech startup stack
Earn bonus points for every second remaining on the clock when you complete the build
After completing the full stack, read the completion message to understand how all 8 layers work together to power a real startup
tips: Start with the layers you are most confident about -- if you know what a database does, place it first to build momentum
Think about the data flow in an app: a user interacts with the UI (frontend), which talks to a server (backend), which reads and writes data (database) -- follow this logical chain
Cloud hosting is the infrastructure that everything runs on -- it is the foundation, not a specific feature like payments or analytics
If you are confused between two slots, read the hints carefully -- they contain specific technical clues that distinguish one layer from another
The CI/CD pipeline is about automation of deployment, not about what the app does for users -- it is a developer tool, not a user-facing feature
Remember: authentication is about identity and security, while payment is about money and transactions -- do not mix these up

minigame_config.description: Build a complete tech startup by dragging the right components into the correct architecture slots. Design a mobile app from frontend to backend, database to deployment.

pieces.label: Frontend UI (React/Flutter)
pieces.description: The frontend is the face of your application -- it is everything the user sees and interacts with. Built using frameworks like React for web apps or Flutter for cross-platform mobile apps, the frontend handles user interface rendering, navigation, animations, and form inputs. It sends requests to the backend API and displays the responses. Companies like Flipkart use React for their web store and Flutter for their mobile app, ensuring a smooth shopping experience across all devices.

pieces.label: Backend API (Node.js/Python)
pieces.description: The backend is the brain of your application -- it processes all the business logic that users never see. Built with frameworks like Express.js (Node.js) or Django/FastAPI (Python), the backend API receives requests from the frontend, validates data, applies business rules, communicates with the database, and returns structured responses. For example, when you search for a restaurant on Zomato, the backend processes your location, filters restaurants, applies sorting algorithms, and returns the results. Without a robust backend, no app can function beyond a static page.

pieces.label: Database (PostgreSQL/MongoDB)
pieces.description: The database is the memory of your application -- it stores all the data your app needs to function. Relational databases like PostgreSQL organise data in structured tables with rows and columns, ideal for financial records, user profiles, and order histories. NoSQL databases like MongoDB store data in flexible JSON-like documents, perfect for rapidly changing data structures. When you save a post on Instagram or a payment record on PhonePe, that data is written to a database. Without a database, your app would forget everything the moment it restarts.

pieces.label: Authentication (OAuth/JWT)
pieces.description: Authentication is the security guard of your application -- it verifies who users are and controls what they can access. OAuth allows users to log in using existing accounts (like Google or Facebook sign-in), while JWT (JSON Web Tokens) creates secure, encrypted session tokens that prove a user's identity on every request. When you log into Paytm with your phone number and OTP, authentication ensures that only you can access your wallet and transaction history. Without authentication, anyone could access anyone else's private data, making the app unsafe and unusable.

pieces.label: Cloud Hosting (AWS/GCP)
pieces.description: Cloud hosting is the foundation and infrastructure of your application -- it provides the servers, storage, and networking that everything else runs on. Providers like Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) offer on-demand computing resources that can scale from serving 10 users to 10 million users without buying a single physical server. Indian startups like Razorpay, Swiggy, and Ola all run on cloud infrastructure, paying only for the resources they use. Cloud hosting also provides global content delivery networks (CDNs), auto-scaling, load balancing, and disaster recovery.

pieces.label: Payment Gateway (Razorpay/Stripe)
pieces.description: The payment gateway is the cash register of your application -- it securely handles all monetary transactions between your users and your business. Payment processors like Razorpay (popular in India) and Stripe (used globally) manage credit card processing, UPI payments, net banking, wallet transactions, and subscription billing. They handle encryption, fraud detection, and compliance with financial regulations like PCI-DSS. When you pay for a Swiggy order using UPI or buy a subscription on Hotstar, the payment gateway processes, validates, and settles the transaction securely.

pieces.label: Analytics Dashboard
pieces.description: The analytics dashboard is the intelligence centre of your application -- it collects, processes, and visualises data about how users interact with your product. It tracks metrics like daily active users (DAU), user retention rates, conversion funnels, revenue per user, session duration, and feature adoption. Tools like Google Analytics, Mixpanel, and custom dashboards built with chart libraries help founders make data-driven decisions. For example, if analytics show that 70% of users drop off at the payment screen, the team knows to redesign that flow. Without analytics, a startup is flying blind.

pieces.label: CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)
pieces.description: The CI/CD pipeline is the automated assembly line of your development process -- it ensures that every code change is automatically tested, built, and deployed to production without manual intervention. CI (Continuous Integration) automatically runs tests and checks every time a developer pushes code to the repository. CD (Continuous Deployment) automatically deploys the validated code to live servers. Tools like GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and GitLab CI enable teams to ship new features multiple times a day with confidence. Without CI/CD, deploying updates would be slow, error-prone, and require manual steps that waste developer time.

slots.label: User Interface Layer
slots.description: This is the topmost layer of the tech stack -- the part that users directly see, touch, and interact with on their screens. It handles rendering visual elements, responding to taps and gestures, and displaying data fetched from the server.
slots.hint: This layer is all about what the user sees on their phone or browser. It uses frameworks like React or Flutter to build interactive screens. Think about which component creates the visual experience.
slots.success_message: Correct! The Frontend UI built with React or Flutter creates the visual interface users interact with. Every button, screen, and animation your users experience is rendered by the frontend layer.
slots.error_message: That is not a user interface component. This slot needs the technology that renders screens, handles user interactions like taps and swipes, and displays data visually on the device.

slots.label: Server Logic Layer
slots.description: This is the processing engine of the application -- it receives requests from the user interface, executes business logic, communicates with the database, and sends back structured responses. It is the invisible brain that powers every feature.
slots.hint: This layer processes requests behind the scenes using server-side frameworks like Node.js or Python. It is the middleman between the frontend and the database. Think about which component handles business logic.
slots.success_message: Correct! The Backend API built with Node.js or Python processes all business logic, handles requests from the frontend, interacts with the database, and returns the results. It is the engine that makes the app actually work.
slots.error_message: That is not a server logic component. This slot needs the technology that runs on the server, processes business rules, handles API requests, and coordinates between the frontend and the database.

slots.label: Data Storage Layer
slots.description: This layer is responsible for persistently storing all application data -- user profiles, orders, messages, preferences, and every piece of information the app needs to remember. Data must be stored reliably and retrieved quickly.
slots.hint: This layer stores and retrieves data permanently using technologies like PostgreSQL or MongoDB. Without it, the app would forget everything when it restarts. Think about which component is responsible for data persistence.
slots.success_message: Correct! The Database (PostgreSQL or MongoDB) stores all your application's data persistently. User accounts, orders, content, and settings are all safely stored and can be queried instantly when needed.
slots.error_message: That is not a data storage component. This slot needs the technology that permanently stores structured data like user profiles, transactions, and content in an organised, queryable format.

slots.label: Security Layer
slots.description: This layer protects the application by verifying user identities and controlling access to resources. It ensures that only legitimate users can access their own data and that sensitive operations require proper authorisation.
slots.hint: This layer handles login, identity verification, and access control using protocols like OAuth and JWT. It prevents unauthorised access to user accounts. Think about which component verifies who a user is.
slots.success_message: Correct! Authentication using OAuth and JWT secures your application by verifying user identities and managing access tokens. It ensures that users can only access their own data and that login sessions are cryptographically secure.
slots.error_message: That is not a security or identity component. This slot needs the technology that handles user login, identity verification, session management, and access control -- not payments or data storage.

slots.label: Infrastructure Layer
slots.description: This is the foundational layer that provides the computing power, storage, and networking upon which every other layer runs. It provides the virtual servers, auto-scaling, load balancing, and global distribution that keep the app fast and available.
slots.hint: This layer provides the servers and computing resources that host your entire application. Providers like AWS and GCP offer scalable infrastructure on demand. Think about which component is the foundation everything else runs on.
slots.success_message: Correct! Cloud Hosting on AWS or GCP provides the infrastructure that powers your entire stack. Virtual servers, auto-scaling, content delivery networks, and managed services all come from the cloud layer, letting you scale from 10 to 10 million users.
slots.error_message: That is not an infrastructure component. This slot needs the technology that provides the actual computing resources -- servers, storage, and networking -- on which all other layers of the application are deployed and run.

slots.label: Monetisation Layer
slots.description: This layer handles all financial transactions within the application -- processing payments from users, managing subscriptions, handling refunds, and ensuring that money flows securely between customers and the business.
slots.hint: This layer processes financial transactions using services like Razorpay or Stripe. It handles UPI, card payments, and subscriptions. Think about which component deals with money and billing.
slots.success_message: Correct! The Payment Gateway (Razorpay or Stripe) processes all monetary transactions securely. It handles UPI payments, credit cards, subscriptions, and refunds while ensuring PCI-DSS compliance and fraud detection to keep financial data safe.
slots.error_message: That is not a monetisation or payment component. This slot needs the technology that processes financial transactions -- credit cards, UPI, subscriptions, and billing -- not user verification or data analytics.

slots.label: Insights Layer
slots.description: This layer collects and visualises data about user behaviour, app performance, and business metrics. It transforms raw event data into actionable insights through charts, dashboards, and reports that help the team make informed decisions.
slots.hint: This layer tracks user behaviour, measures KPIs, and displays metrics on visual dashboards. It helps founders understand what users are doing and make data-driven decisions. Think about which component provides business intelligence.
slots.success_message: Correct! The Analytics Dashboard tracks every meaningful user interaction and business metric. From daily active users to conversion funnels and revenue trends, analytics provide the data-driven insights that help startups iterate and grow.
slots.error_message: That is not an analytics or insights component. This slot needs the technology that tracks user behaviour, measures business metrics, and presents data through visual dashboards and reports -- not deployment automation or payment processing.

slots.label: Deployment Layer
slots.description: This layer automates the process of taking code changes from a developer's machine all the way to the live production environment. It runs automated tests, builds the application, and deploys it without any manual steps.
slots.hint: This layer automates testing and deployment using tools like GitHub Actions. It ensures that every code change is automatically tested and shipped to production. Think about which component handles the delivery pipeline from code to live servers.
slots.success_message: Correct! The CI/CD Pipeline using GitHub Actions automates your entire release process. Every code push is automatically tested, built, and deployed to production, enabling your team to ship features rapidly and reliably without manual deployment steps.
slots.error_message: That is not a deployment automation component. This slot needs the technology that automates the software delivery pipeline -- running tests, building artifacts, and deploying code to production servers automatically.

minigame_config.completion_message: Congratulations -- you have assembled a complete tech startup stack! Here is how all 8 layers work together in a real application: When a user opens your app, the Frontend UI (React/Flutter) renders the interface on their device. Every tap and interaction sends a request to the Backend API (Node.js/Python), which processes the business logic. The backend reads and writes data to the Database (PostgreSQL/MongoDB), ensuring nothing is lost. The Authentication layer (OAuth/JWT) verifies the user's identity on every request, keeping accounts secure. All of this runs on Cloud Hosting (AWS/GCP), which provides the servers, auto-scaling, and global distribution to handle millions of users. When the user makes a purchase, the Payment Gateway (Razorpay/Stripe) processes the transaction securely. Meanwhile, the Analytics Dashboard silently tracks user behaviour and business metrics, giving the founding team the insights they need to improve the product. And every time a developer writes new code, the CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions) automatically tests it, builds it, and deploys it to production within minutes. This is exactly how Indian tech startups like Razorpay, Zerodha, CRED, and Meesho are built -- layer by layer, each component playing a critical role in delivering a seamless product to millions of users.

psychological_skills: Systems Thinking -- understanding how multiple interdependent components work together as a unified system, rather than viewing them in isolation
Logical Reasoning -- analysing the function of each technology component and matching it to the correct architectural role based on its capabilities
Pattern Recognition -- identifying commonalities between real-world apps (Zomato, Paytm, Swiggy) and the abstract tech stack layers they are built upon
Decision Making Under Pressure -- evaluating options and making correct placements within a time constraint, simulating real-world project deadlines
Technical Literacy -- building foundational vocabulary and conceptual understanding of software architecture that prepares students for careers in technology
Analytical Thinking -- breaking down a complex system (a tech startup) into its constituent layers and understanding the responsibility of each
Entrepreneurial Mindset -- understanding the complete technology foundation required to launch a digital product, fostering startup thinking and innovation

glossary_terms.definition: The complete set of technologies, frameworks, programming languages, and tools used to build and run a software application. A typical tech stack includes a frontend framework, backend language, database, hosting infrastructure, and supporting services.
glossary_terms.example: The MERN stack (MongoDB, Express.js, React, Node.js) is a popular full-stack JavaScript tech stack used by startups to build web applications quickly because all layers use the same programming language.

glossary_terms.definition: A set of rules and protocols that allows different software applications to communicate with each other. The backend exposes APIs that the frontend calls to send and receive data. APIs use standard formats like JSON and protocols like REST or GraphQL.
glossary_terms.example: When the Swiggy app shows you nearby restaurants, the frontend sends a request to the backend API with your location. The API processes the request, queries the database for restaurants in your area, and returns the results as structured data.

glossary_terms.definition: The delivery of computing services -- including servers, storage, databases, networking, and software -- over the internet ('the cloud') on a pay-as-you-go basis, rather than owning and maintaining physical hardware.
glossary_terms.example: Indian startups like Ola and Razorpay use AWS cloud computing to run their applications. During peak hours like IPL matches or festival sales, cloud auto-scaling automatically adds more servers to handle the surge in traffic.

glossary_terms.definition: A software development practice where code changes are automatically tested (CI) and deployed to production servers (CD) through an automated pipeline. This eliminates manual deployment steps and reduces the risk of human error.
glossary_terms.example: When a developer at CRED pushes a bug fix to GitHub, the CI/CD pipeline automatically runs 500 unit tests, builds the application, and if all tests pass, deploys the fix to production servers within 15 minutes -- without any manual intervention.

glossary_terms.definition: Authentication is the process of verifying a user's identity (who are you?), while authorisation determines what resources they are allowed to access (what can you do?). Together, they form the security backbone of any application.
glossary_terms.example: When you log into Paytm using your phone number and OTP, that is authentication (proving you are you). When the app then allows you to view your wallet balance but prevents you from accessing another user's account, that is authorisation (controlling access).

glossary_terms.definition: A technology service that processes online payment transactions by securely transmitting payment information between the customer, the merchant's application, and the financial institutions (banks, card networks). It handles encryption, fraud detection, and regulatory compliance.
glossary_terms.example: Razorpay, an Indian payment gateway, processes over 500 million transactions annually. When you pay for a Zomato order via UPI, Razorpay validates the transaction, communicates with your bank, confirms the payment, and notifies Zomato -- all within seconds.

win_conditions.description: Place all 8 tech stack components in the correct architecture slots within 3 minutes to build a fully functional startup tech stack! Fewer wrong placements mean a higher score. Complete the full stack to see how frontend, backend, database, security, cloud, payments, analytics, and deployment all work together to power a real tech startup.
